title: Cinderella Goes to the Ball

before.title: Cinderella Goes to the Ball
before.text:
Cinderella lived with her stepmother and two stepsisters. They gave her all the hardest work in the house.

One day, the family received an invitation to a royal ball. Cinderella wanted to go, but her stepmother refused.

After the others left, Cinderella sat alone and cried.

Then help came in a magical way. Cinderella received a beautiful dress, glass shoes, and a carriage.

There was one important rule. She had to return before midnight.

At the ball, no one recognized Cinderella. The prince asked her to dance, and they spent the evening together.

Cinderella was so happy that she forgot the time.

Then the clock began to strike twelve.

She ran from the palace as fast as she could. On the stairs, one glass shoe fell from her foot.

Cinderella could not stop to pick it up.

The prince found the shoe after she disappeared. He decided to search the kingdom for the person who could wear it.

title: Rapunzel Plans a Way Out

before.title: Rapunzel in the Tower
before.text:
Rapunzel lived in a tall tower deep in the forest. The tower had no door and no stairs.

Only one person visited her. An old woman came to the tower and called Rapunzel from below.

Rapunzel had very long hair. She lowered it from the window, and the woman climbed up.

For many years, Rapunzel believed this was the only life she could have.

Then a young prince heard her singing in the forest.

He watched the tower from a distance and saw how the old woman entered.

The next evening, the prince came to the tower and used the same call.

Rapunzel was frightened when a stranger appeared at her window. But the prince spoke kindly.

He told her about towns, rivers, markets, and roads beyond the forest.

Rapunzel listened with great interest. She had seen almost none of the world.

After that, the prince returned many times.

Slowly, Rapunzel began to imagine a life outside the tower.

after.title: Rapunzel Plans a Way Out
after.text:
Rapunzel lived in a high tower with no door or stairs. An old woman visited by calling from below. Rapunzel let down her long hair, and the woman climbed up.

One day, a prince heard Rapunzel singing in the forest. He saw how the woman reached the window. When he returned, he used the same call. Rapunzel was frightened at first, but they talked, and he came back another day.

Rapunzel wanted to leave the tower. She asked the prince to bring her lengths of silk. She would tie them into a ladder and climb down when it was strong enough.

Each visit gave her more silk. The ladder was not ready yet, but Rapunzel had begun making a way out.

reason: The prince’s repeated account of markets and roads is invented. Preserve the hair-entry scene but add Rapunzel’s own idea for a silk ladder from the Grimm source.

title: Snow White Finds a Small House

before.title: Snow White Finds a Small House
before.text:
Snow White ran through the forest until she was too tired to continue.

As evening came, she saw a small house among the trees.

Inside, everything was tiny. There were seven small chairs, seven plates, and seven beds.

Snow White was hungry, so she ate a little food from each plate. Then she lay across several beds and fell asleep.

Later, seven miners returned home from work.

They were surprised to find someone in their house.

When Snow White woke up, she was afraid. But the miners spoke gently and asked why she was alone.

She told them that she could not safely return home.

The miners agreed to let her stay.

“You may live here,” they said, “but be careful when we are away.”

Snow White thanked them.

The next morning, the miners left for work. Snow White watched them disappear into the forest.

For the first time in many days, she felt safe. But she did not know that danger was still searching for her.

after.title: Snow White Finds a Small House
after.text:
Snow White ran through the forest until she was too tired to continue. At evening, she found a small house among the trees.

Inside were seven small chairs, seven plates and seven beds. She ate a little food from each plate. She tried the beds until she found one that fit, and she fell asleep.

Seven dwarfs returned from work in the hills. They noticed that someone had eaten their food. Then one of them found Snow White asleep.

In the morning, she told them why she could not return home. The dwarfs let her stay but warned her to be careful while they were away. Snow White watched them leave. She felt safe in the small house, though danger had not gone away.

reason: The source calls the seven hosts dwarfs and puts Snow White to sleep in the seventh bed after trying the others. Correct these details and retain this episode only.

title: Alice Follows the White Rabbit

before.title: Alice Follows the White Rabbit
before.text:
Alice was sitting outside with her sister when she noticed a white rabbit.

Seeing a rabbit was not strange. But this rabbit wore a coat and carried a watch.

“I am late!” the rabbit said.

Alice had never heard a rabbit speak before.

She jumped up and followed it across the field.

The rabbit reached a large hole under a hedge and disappeared inside.

Alice did not stop to think. She went into the hole after it.

Instead of falling quickly, she moved slowly through a deep tunnel.

She passed shelves, pictures, and strange objects along the walls.

Alice had enough time to wonder where she was going.

At last, she landed safely at the bottom.

Ahead of her, the white rabbit hurried around a corner.

Alice followed and entered a long hall filled with doors.

The rabbit was gone.

Alice looked around the hall. Her ordinary afternoon had suddenly become a very unusual adventure.

title: Alice and the Little Bottle

before.title: Alice Drinks from the Little Bottle
before.text:
Alice stood in a long hall with many locked doors.

On a glass table, she found a small golden key. It opened a tiny door behind a curtain.

Through the door, Alice could see a beautiful garden.

There was one problem. The door was much too small for her.

Alice returned to the table and noticed a little bottle.

A label on it told her to drink.

Alice was careful. She checked the bottle and smelled it before taking a small taste.

Soon, something strange happened.

She began to grow smaller.

Alice was pleased at first. Now she could fit through the tiny door.

Then she remembered the key.

She had left it on top of the glass table, which now seemed very high.

Alice tried to reach it, but she could not.

She sat down and felt frustrated.

Getting smaller had solved one problem and created another.

Alice began to understand that in this strange place, every answer could bring a new question.

after.title: Alice and the Little Bottle
after.text:
Alice stood in a hall with many locked doors. A small key on a glass table opened a tiny door. Through it, she saw a beautiful garden, but she was too large to enter.

Back at the table, she found a bottle labeled “DRINK ME.” She looked for a warning that said “poison.” She saw none. In this strange story, she drank from the bottle and began to grow smaller.

Now Alice was small enough for the door. Then she remembered the key. She had left it on the high table. She could see the garden but could no longer reach the key.

reason: The source says Alice checked for a poison label, not that smelling the unknown bottle established safety. Retell the check without presenting it as a reliable test; preserve the forgotten key.

title: What a Cat’s Purr Tells Us

before.title: Why Cats Purr
before.text: A cat makes a purr by moving parts near its voice box very quickly. Air passes through, and we hear a low, steady sound. Cats often purr when they are warm and safe, such as when a person strokes them. They may also purr when they are hurt, afraid, or resting after stress. This means the sound does not always show happiness. It may help a cat stay calm or ask for gentle contact. People enjoy the sound, but researchers are still learning all the reasons cats make it.

after.title: What a Cat’s Purr Tells Us
after.text:
A cat can make a low sound called a purr. It comes from vibrations in the area of the voice box while the cat breathes.

A cat may purr when it rests beside a person. It may also purr when it is frightened or unwell. The sound alone cannot tell us that the cat is happy.

People who care for a cat look at more than one sign. They watch how it moves, eats and reacts to touch. Researchers are still studying exactly how cats make a purr and why they use it in different situations.

reason: Purring can occur in varied contexts; the mechanism is complex and “helps a cat stay calm” is not established by the cited physiology. Limit the description to production and observation.

title: Pinocchio Runs Away from Home

before.title: Pinocchio Runs Away from Home
before.text:
Geppetto made Pinocchio from wood and hoped the boy would become kind and responsible.

Pinocchio had other ideas.

He wanted excitement, and he did not enjoy being told what to do.

Soon after learning to walk, Pinocchio ran out of the house.

He raced through the street while Geppetto followed him.

People stopped to watch the strange wooden boy.

Pinocchio thought running away was great fun. He did not understand why Geppetto looked worried.

Before long, a policeman stopped them.

The situation became confusing, and Geppetto was taken away for a short time.

Pinocchio returned home alone.

At first, he enjoyed the quiet house. No one was there to give him rules.

Then night came.

The room felt cold and empty. Pinocchio had no food, and there was no one to help him.

For the first time, he began to think about what Geppetto had done for him.

Being free was not as simple as he had imagined.

title: The Crow and the Hard Nut

before.title: The Clever Crow's Trick
before.text: A crow found a hard nut but could not open it with its beak. The bird carried the nut above a road and dropped it. A car passed, but the nut did not break. The crow tried again and placed it near a wheel mark. This time, a car cracked the shell. The bird waited on a light until the road was clear, then flew down to eat. It had used the cars as tools and the light as a safe signal. Careful watching had solved the problem.

after.title: The Crow and the Hard Nut
after.text:
This is an imagined crow story. The crow found a hard nut beside a road. It dropped the nut from a branch, but the shell stayed closed.

Next, the bird let the nut fall onto the road. A car passed over it. The crow waited on a tree branch until the road was empty.

When it flew down, it found the shell cracked. It ate the nut and carried the empty shell away. The story shows one way an animal might use things in its surroundings.

reason: The specific crow’s choices and traffic-light intention are invented; the evidence on car-assisted nut cracking is not enough to treat this exact event as observation. Label it fiction and avoid suggesting a person approach traffic.

title: Bats Hunt After Sunset

before.title: Bat's Nighttime Feast
before.text: Bats slept in a barn during the day. At sunset, they flew over the fields to hunt small insects. They did not need daylight to find them. Each bat sent out very high sounds and listened for the sound that came back. The returning sound showed where an insect was moving. In one night, the group ate many insects that could have harmed crops. The farmers rarely saw the work, but the night hunters helped protect the fields.

after.title: Bats Hunt After Sunset
after.text:
Some insect-eating bats rest in a barn by day. At sunset, they leave to search over nearby fields.

Many of these bats send out sounds too high for people to hear. The sounds bounce back from objects, including insects. A bat listens to the returning sounds as it flies and hunts.

Some insects are pests in fields. Bats can eat them, but this short example does not tell us how many insects they eat or how much a farmer's crop changes. The bats also use their eyes and other senses.

reason: The claim about all bats and protecting crops is too broad. Describe insect-eating bats and frame crop effects as possible rather than an observed result for invented farmers.

title: A Room for the Town

before.title: Town's First Community Center
before.text:
This is a made-up policy example based on choices real communities may face.

A town had no warm place where people could meet in winter. An empty shop stood near the station, so several neighbors asked to use it. Families painted the walls. A carpenter fixed the tables, and students collected books and games. The town paid for heat and lights. Soon, children studied there after school, older people held classes, and local groups planned events. The center began with an unused room, but it grew because many people gave time, skills, or small gifts.

after.title: A Room for the Town
after.text:
This town is imagined. In winter, neighbors needed a warm place to meet. An empty shop near the station seemed useful, but it needed work.

The town checked the building and agreed to try it as a meeting room. Staff arranged heat and lights. A carpenter repaired some tables, and neighbors brought books and games.

For the first month, the room opened on two afternoons a week. Students used a table after school, and an older group met there to play cards. The town counted visits and asked people what hours they needed next.

reason: The town and policy are explicitly invented, so classify narrative fiction. Show approval and a limited trial before claims of lasting community use.
